topIssues.title: flake: reth-optimism-node integration test peers_negotiate_eth_69 SIGSEGVs on teardown
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filed on behalf of @ajsutton.

## Test

`reth-optimism-node::it p2p_version::peers_negotiate_eth_69` — `rust/op-reth/crates/node/tests/it/p2p_version.rs`

## CI evidence

- Job: https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/126050/workflows/6f052c6e-19a6-47dc-9a51-6e6f03473058/jobs/5100649
- Workflow: `rust-ci-gate-short` / `op-reth-integration-tests`
- Triggered on merge-queue branch for PR #20963

## Symptom

The test's assertions all pass — nextest reports:

```
test p2p_version::peers_negotiate_eth_69 ... ok
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 7 filtered out; finished in 5.13s
(test aborted with signal 11: SIGSEGV)
```

The crash is during process teardown after the test body returns Ok. Nextest marks the run as failed because the binary exited with a signal, killing the merge-queue check.

## Suspected area

The test spins up two op-reth nodes via `reth_optimism_node::utils::setup(2)` and queries the admin RPC to confirm peers negotiate eth/69. The body completes cleanly; the SIGSEGV happens as the tokio runtime / p2p stack / native networking resources are dropped at process exit.

## Reported occurrences

This flake has been observed on multiple recent runs (per @ajsutton). No prior `C-flake` issue existed for this test.

## Next step

Investigation underway via op-claude flake-fixer agent.

topIssues.title: Enumerate forks programmatically
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
Right now, forks and their schedules are typically struct fiends. This results in a schema change every time a fork is added, which requires tedious, error-prone updates across the codebase.

We should only have to update a line or two in a single file to add a fork and its metadata (or perhaps only the superchain registry, in an ideal world).

topIssues.title: op-core/superchain is unconsumable by downstream Go modules: superchain-configs.zip is gitignored
topIssues.author: jefr90
topIssues.body:
`op-core/superchain` embeds `superchain-configs.zip`, which is gitignored and generated locally from the superchain-registry submodule. The zip is therefore absent from the published Go module, and any downstream module that reaches this package fails to compile:

```
op-core/superchain/chain.go:21:12: pattern superchain-configs.zip: no matching files found
```

### Verification

- The zip is gitignored at every release tag checked: `op-node/v1.17.0`, `v1.18.0`, `v1.19.0`, `v1.19.5`, `op-contracts/v7.0.0`, `op-contracts/v8.0.0-rc.3`. Only `superchain-configs.zip.sha256` is committed.
- The published module confirms it. `$GOMODCACHE/github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism@v1.19.5/op-core/superchain/` contains `superchain-configs.zip.sha256` but no `superchain-configs.zip`.
- `op-core/superchain/sync-superchain.sh` documents three modes (verify, refresh, external). All three require a superchain-registry checkout, so none is usable by a module consumer. There is no consumer-facing README.

The monorepo does not hit this itself because `just build-superchain-go` runs as a build prerequisite, and container builds carry `melange/pipelines/op-stack-go/sync-superchain.yaml`, whose comment documents this exact failure. Neither helps a downstream `go build`.

### Impact

Every OP Stack release from 2026-04-29 onward, when `op-core/superchain` was introduced in #20314, is unconsumable as a plain Go dependency by anything that reaches this package.

Found while upgrading `ethereum-optimism/supersim`, which reaches it via `genesis/worldgen` -> `op-chain-ops/interopgen` -> `op-core/superchain`. supersim had to pin `op-node/v1.16.13` (2026-04-21), the last release before the change, instead of the current one. See ethereum-optimism/supersim#424.

### Possible directions

1. Commit the zip. Simplest, at the cost of a binary in the tree.
2. Make the embed optional behind a build tag, with a runtime loader as the fallback for consumers that do not need the built-in configs.
3. Publish the bundle as a separate versioned Go module or artifact that consumers can depend on.

Happy to take direction on which is preferred.

topPRs.title: op-reth,kona: implement sequencer-defined fees
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
## Description

Implement Sequencer-Defined Fees (SDF) at Lagoon. The sequencer selects `baseFeePerGas` through a pluggable policy, commits that selection in the trailing `PostExec` transaction, and validators reproduce execution from the committed fee without running producer policy.

This change:

- extends the unactivated version-1 `PostExec` payload with the selected base fee
- requires a trailing Lagoon commitment, including for empty refund sets
- wires fee selection and immutable per-payload caching through op-reth payload building
- uses selected-fee quotes in txpool, pending execution, and fee-related RPC paths
- validates Lagoon commitments on Engine API block import
- reproduces fallback commitments in Kona and preserves them in output artifacts
- applies selected fees during flashblock replay and reserves block space for the mandatory commitment
- updates public documentation and acceptance-test expectations

L1 data fees, operator fees, batch formats, and payload-attribute schemas are unchanged.

## Dependencies

- Depends on ethereum-optimism/reth#8. The Rust workspace is pinned to that PR's organization-owned branch revision while it is under review.
- Specification: ethereum-optimism/specs#934.
- Premium policy integration: ethereum-optimism/optimism-premium#222.

## Validation

Completed before opening this draft:

- full Go lint and Optimism Rust lint on the initial series
- targeted op-reth/Kona tests, including 41 Kona executor tests
- no-std checks and nightly formatting
- focused checks for consensus, Kona executor/driver, flashblocks, payload builder, and RPC against the public reth revision
- regression tests for Engine API commitment validation, Kona fallback transaction persistence, flashblock selected-fee execution, and block-size reservation

Final review, broader validation after the latest fixes, and CI follow-up are still in progress.

## Review notes

Earlier independent review findings about the Engine API validation path, Kona fallback artifacts, flashblock fees, historical fee history, fill-transaction defaults, and block-size accounting were addressed before this draft was opened.

Dismissed findings:

- Cached policy failures are intentional: a payload ID has one immutable policy resolution across retries.
- A `PostExec` version 2 is unnecessary because version 1 has not activated onchain.
- Extending op-geth is out of scope because Lagoon follows the op-geth support horizon.
- No span-batch format change is required; span batches already transport the transaction bytes.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1-proposer: enforce complete parent ancestry
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- separate parent eligibility from retained game lifecycle state and quarantine the complete known descendant closure when any ancestor becomes blacklisted, retired, or terminally invalid
- refresh pinned standing, exclude incomplete cached ancestry, and recheck a consistent latest lineage snapshot immediately before creation and proof submission
- preserve directly disallowed creator refunds through resolution, distribution-mode selection, DelayedWETH unlock, payout, and final lifecycle eviction
- retain structural parents while cached, pending, active, in-flight, unseen, or future contract-valid descendants can still depend on them

Closes #22784.

## Test plan

- red/green: `dynamic_disallowed_ancestor_marks_descendants_parent_ineligible_without_lifecycle_loss` failed on the baseline because subtree invalidation removed lifecycle records, then passed with the fix
- targeted ancestry, submission-race, refund, parent-retention, anchor-rotation, reverse-discovery, incomplete-lineage, and stale-identity regressions
- `mise exec -- cargo nextest run --release --package kona-sp1-proposer --all-features` (192 passed)
- `mise exec -- just f`
- `mise exec -- just l`
- `mise exec -- just lint-go`

topPRs.title: contracts: prove withdrawal air gap transition closure
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Overview

Adds Kontrol proofs for the end-to-end withdrawal authorization timing chain, dispute-game outcome finality, Portal transition closure, and ETHLockbox value accounting.

### Composed air-gap theorem

For a withdrawal proven at `T_proof` against a game that favorably resolves at `T_resolve`, successful Portal authorization implies:

`T_finalize > T_proof + PROOF_MATURITY_DELAY_SECONDS`

and

`T_finalize > T_resolve + DISPUTE_GAME_FINALITY_DELAY_SECONDS`

Both inequalities are strict because the production contracts reject their equality boundaries. The proof composes production `OptimismPortal2.checkWithdrawal` and `AnchorStateRegistry.isGameClaimValid` logic.

### One-preparatory-call transition closure

Seven new Kontrol cases execute every current non-finalization state-changing Portal entry path from an attacker contract:

- `depositTransaction`
- `donateETH`
- raw ETH `receive()`
- `initialize`
- `migrateLiquidity`
- `migrateToSharedDisputeGame`
- `proveWithdrawalTransaction`

After the preparatory call succeeds or reverts, each case proves that the target withdrawal still has the same proven game and proof timestamp, remains unfinalized, retains the same AnchorStateRegistry and default `l2Sender`, and remains backed by a `CHALLENGER_WINS` game with the same `resolvedAt`.

Each case then executes both production finalization entry points:

- `finalizeWithdrawalTransaction`
- `finalizeWithdrawalTransactionExternalProof`

Both must fail, and the finalized bit must remain false. Calls share the same L1 timestamp, so this directly models a prep call plus finalization bundled atomically by an attacker contract.

The game factory harness implements `gameAtIndex`, allowing the withdrawal-proving path to receive the challenger-backed game before the Portal rejects it.

### ABI and mutability coverage

The Kontrol job hashes the complete production ABI for the Portal and all five covered game families. CI fails if a new selector appears or if an existing getter changes from view to state-mutating. Raw `receive()` is covered by a dedicated proof.

This means a new `allowThisWithdrawalToFinalize(bytes32)`-style method cannot silently fall outside the proof inventory: its addition fails the manifest check until the ABI hash and transition proof are reviewed together.

### Supporting invariants

- FaultDisputeGame, PermissionedDisputeGame, SuperFaultDisputeGame, and ZKDisputeGame favorable resolution atomically stores `DEFENDER_WINS` and `resolvedAt = block.timestamp`
- SuperPermissionedDisputeGame initialization atomically stores `DEFENDER_WINS`, `createdAt = block.timestamp`, and `resolvedAt = createdAt`
- all five game families preserve a stored `CHALLENGER_WINS` outcome and resolution timestamp through later resolution attempts
- AnchorStateRegistry validity implies a nonzero favorable resolution timestamp strictly older than its finality delay
- AnchorStateRegistry never validates a `CHALLENGER_WINS` game at any later symbolic timestamp
- Portal proof maturity remains independently required even if the registry authorizes a game
- ETHLockbox unlock debits exactly the requested symbolic value, and unlock/relock restores balances exactly

## Scope and assumptions

The transition proofs cover exactly one current preparatory Portal call followed by finalization, using canonical calldata and one concrete attacker contract. They do not claim universal coverage of arbitrary-length call sequences or every possible argument tuple. The ABI manifest prevents a newly introduced mutator or mutability change from being accepted without explicit review and proof coverage.

The theorem also assumes:

- Portal, AnchorStateRegistry, factory, and registered game implementations remain fixed during the interval, or their upgrade/admin keys remain secure
- clone immutable arguments and existing clone implementation addresses remain fixed
- L1 `block.timestamp` is the common monotonic clock
- pause/unpause is a trusted operational control
- registration, respect, retirement, and blacklist predicates have their valid values for successful authorization

It does not claim safety if the registry or game code is arbitrarily compromised, and it does not claim global ETHLockbox solvency across every authorized Portal.

## Verification

Pinned `runtimeverificationinc/kontrol:ubuntu-jammy-1.0.90`:

- 7/7 new preparatory-call plus finalization proofs passed, 0 failed
- full production ABI coverage check passed in the pinned container
- 5 challenger-terminality proofs passed
- 5 favorable-resolution/current-timestamp proofs passed
- registry validity and challenger-invalidity proofs passed
- composed Portal plus registry dual-air-gap theorem passed
- Portal proof-maturity and registry trust-boundary proofs passed
- 2 symbolic ETHLockbox accounting proofs passed

Repository checks:

- full multi-version `forge build` passed during branch validation
- final focused proof build passed
- `forge fmt --check` passed
- Forge test-name validation passed
- unused-import validation passed
- shell checks passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## CI note

The selected op-deployer image build succeeds, then its non-required provenance-attestation step fails because fork-origin PRs are not granted `id-token: write`. Prior commits failed at the identical unrelated attestation step; required checks pass.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1-proposer: reject pending game ancestry
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Known pending parents now make cached descendants ineligible for proving or extension, while unknown historical cache gaps retain the existing fail-open behavior. Stale pending branches are tombstoned and cleared atomically; if one is later promoted to the registry anchor, the proposer performs a bounded in-cycle factory rescan against the same pinned L1 view before planning work.

Regression coverage includes pending ancestry, stale eviction, same-index reorg replacement, and anchor recovery. All 253 `kona-sp1-proposer` tests, nightly Rustfmt, and proposer-local Clippy pass; workspace-wide lint was not completed because the fresh worktree lacks the `superchain-registry` submodule and dependency-inclusive Clippy encounters a pre-existing `kona-derive` warning.

Related: #22787

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: bump OPCMv2 to v9 and retire anchor-root overrides
topPRs.author: 0xOneTony
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Bumps OPCMv2 to `9.0.0`, activating the missing-lockbox deployment allowance introduced in #22805.

Retires the starting-anchor-root override. Upgrades preserve the chain’s existing anchor instead of accepting a replacement.

**Changes**

- Keeps ETHLockbox deployment permission restricted to v9.
- Removes the retired override from upgrade callers, fork setup, and migration tests.
- Runs missing-lockbox tests against the actual OPCM version while retaining version-boundary coverage.
- Checks preservation of existing lockboxes, balances, anchor roots, and anchor games.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22836
